public_social_counterweight.note: The Permanent Fund and PFD are real common-wealth rails, but the dividend amount and fiscal draw rules are not enough to guarantee a floor.

lower_half_real_floor.note: A $1,000-style dividend helps liquidity but is too small and volatile to substitute for housing, energy, health, care, and climate/disaster risk floors.

early_foothold_open_access.note: Universal cash can help early footholds, but adequacy depends on household size, remoteness, costs, and whether payment timing matches threshold moments.

parent_backed_threshold_dependency.note: Need data on whether dividend reduces family-backed threshold dependence.

group_person_closure.note: Eligibility boundaries, children, formerly incarcerated people, Indigenous communities, and high-cost rural households need separate reads.

housing_land_washout.note: High costs, energy/hazard exposure, repairs, insurance, and remote-market constraints can wash out annual cash-dividend gains.

debt_fee_washout.note: Need data on garnishment, debt collection, and use for arrears.

wealth_to_rule_risk.note: Fund governance can be strong while broader state wealth order remains unscored.

ownership_legibility.note: Fund assets and PFD eligibility are legible compared with opaque private wealth, but governance, formula, fiscal politics, and intergenerational claims need continuing review.

climate_insurance_drag.note: Alaska-specific climate/infrastructure cost pressure should be tested separately.

monetary_asset_price_channel.note: Fund returns and state budget debates can be affected by global asset prices.

case_notes: This case demonstrates that a genuine common-wealth claim is not automatically a real-floor pass.

evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track statutory formula, appropriations, ERA draw, budget tradeoffs, and annual dividend setting.

gate_07_public_common_counterweight.why: The Alaska PFD is a genuine person-level public-wealth rail, but it earns only a watch/provisional status until adequacy, eligibility, formula stability, and service-floor interaction are proven.

gate_02_floor_reality.why: A cash dividend does not by itself prove the real floor because costs, climate, remoteness, and household needs can exceed the annual claim.
